## Idea
UNRELEASED SOURCE: this entry requires the protected implementation at 329c914413af5c16694b6abb488f1e4c6bab6b9f. The public FS.GG.Algorithms 0.2.0 package does not contain UtilityAi. Bounded Q16.16 scores, monotone response curves and stable first-on-tie selection form a pure deterministic utility decision kernel.

## Complexity
score/value/evaluate/invert have fixed-width bounded work. product and choose scan n inputs in O(n) time and O(1) extra space; loops do not grow the call stack.

## Use when
A caller has already normalized considerations and wants reproducible utility scoring and action selection, with effects handled elsewhere.

## Avoid when
Only public0.2.0 is available, inputs require implicit normalization, or a weighted/compensated utility policy is required. Those are not this source contract.

## Pitfalls
Input Fixed values clamp to0..1. Quadratic uses Fixed nearest/ties-up multiply; square root uses floor square root. product rounds after every multiply: reordering/reassociation can change the result. Empty product is1; zero vetoes. choose keeps the first action even when all scores are0; empty actions give None. Caller action order must be deterministic; no random or policy tie-break is implicit.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms, UNRELEASED SOURCE at the protected revision above; this example was checked against that source, not the public0.2.0 package.
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Decision.UtilityAi.choose: ('Action * UtilityScore) list -> ('Action * UtilityScore) option`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Numerics
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Decision
let value = Fixed.ofRatio 3 4
let desire = UtilityAi.evaluate UtilityCurve.Quadratic value
let fallback = UtilityAi.score Fixed.half
let selected = UtilityAi.choose ["act", desire; "wait", fallback]
```

## Tests
UtilityAiTests at the cited protected revision checks bounded/monotone curves, endpoint/clamping behaviour, rounded product, ordered first-on-tie choice and independent model agreement. The library owner's original .NET/JavaScript fixture proof includes13 Utility cases in its178-case corpus; this pack does not rerun or infer publication from that proof.
